title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to Grothendieck's 'équation des lacets' manuscripts. Notation, as far as it can be inferred from this and the neighbouring pages:

- Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞}, generated by inertia loops l_0, l_1, l_∞ with l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1.
- M_{0,3}^{!~} is a group of automorphisms of Π̂_{0,3}, presumably a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group. M^{!~}_{0,3}[0] = Norm(L_0) is the subgroup normalizing the inertia subgroup L_0 = ⟨l_0⟩.
- φ̂ : Π̂_{0,3} → Ŝ^+_{0,3} is a homomorphism to a profinite completion of what is evidently PSL_2(Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3. It sends l_0 ↦ ε_0 (the parabolic element), l_∞ ↦ ρ^{-1} (ρ of order 3) and l_1 to an element of order 2. This is the profinite version of the λ-line → j-line orbifold map M_{0,4} → M_{1,1}.
- Ŝ_{0,3} = Ŝ^+_{0,3}·{1, τ_∞} adds an orientation-reversing involution (a PGL_2(Z)-type extension).
- σ_∞ is the order-2 element, with ρ = σ_∞ ε_0.
- τ'_∞ is the conjugate/variant of τ_∞, apparently τ'_∞ = σ_∞ τ_∞.

Problem. On the previous page Grothendieck introduces Φ(u·a) = u φ̂(a). It is a group homomorphism precisely because elements u ∈ M^{!~}_{0,3}[0] commute with φ̂ effectively, not only up to inner automorphisms. He wants to compare this Φ with the one of §41 explicitly. Here he returns to determining the u_λ that commute with φ̂, i.e. satisfy the commutation relation (5) with λ = 1. This is the condition for an element of the GT-like group to descend compatibly along the λ-line → j-line map, i.e. to act on \hat{PSL_2(Z)}.

Step 1. Because u_λ normalizes L_0 with u(l_0) = l_0^λ, the relation (5) at x = l_0 is tautological: both sides equal ε_0^λ. Since l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1, it suffices to impose (5) at x = l_1 or at x = l_∞.

Step 2. At x = l_1 one gets his condition (1D). He finds it remarkable because it computes the 'delicate' parameter β from the 'coarse' parameter γ. The general existence of β in terms of γ 'rests on foundations not yet established'. Here, in addition, a Z/nZ-type invariant is easily determined from γ.

Step 3. He decides instead to write (5) at x = l_∞. As a preliminary he proves (4∞): τ'_∞(ρ) = ρ^{-1}. The computation is τ'_∞(ρ) = σ_∞(τ_∞ ρ) = σ_∞(l_0^{-1}ρ), which gives ε_0^{-1}·σ_∞ρσ_∞^{-1} = ε_0^{-1}σ_∞^{-1} = ρ^{-1}, using ρ = σ_∞ε_0. So τ'_∞ acts as inversion on the order-3 generator.

Continuation (next page). If u(ρ) = ρ^μ then μ ≡ ±1 mod 3, so u(ρ) = τ'^{α_3}_∞(ρ). Condition (5) at l_∞ then becomes: τ'^{α_3}_∞ φ̂(f_∞) α centralizes ρ in Ŝ_{0,3}.
errors: The written chain for τ'_∞(ρ) is partly crossed out and compressed; the intermediate equality σ_∞(l_0^{-1}ρ) = ε_0^{-1}σ_∞ρσ_∞^{-1} silently identifies l_0 with its image ε_0 and uses σ_∞ρσ_∞^{-1} = σ_∞^{-1} (since ρ = σ_∞ε_0 and σ_∞^2 = 1). This is correct with those conventions but not written out.
The symbol written 'φ' inside τ'_∞(φ) should be ρ, as the conclusion ρ^{-1} shows.
The tautology check at x = l_0 writes exponent 'H' (as transcribed); it should be λ (here λ = 1). With that reading the check is correct.

ideas.what: Reduction of the commutation condition u∘φ̂ = φ̂∘u to a single generator (l_1 or l_∞), since it holds automatically on l_0 for elements normalizing inertia at 0
ideas.modern_name: compatibility of the GT action with the λ-line → j-line map / action of GT on profinite PSL_2(Z)
ideas.where_published: Theme of the Esquisse (Teichmüller tower, M_{1,1}) without these computations

ideas.what: τ'_∞ acts by inversion on the order-3 elliptic generator ρ; hence any u with u(ρ) = ρ^μ has μ ≡ ±1 mod 3
ideas.modern_name: outer action of PGL_2(Z) on PSL_2(Z) ≅ Z/2*Z/3; mod-3 cyclotomic character component

ideas.what: Remark that the commutation condition expresses the 'delicate' parameter β in terms of the 'coarse' parameter γ, whose general existence depends on unestablished foundations
ideas.modern_name: determination of the f-component of a GT element from compatibility constraints (relations I/II-type)

missed.claim: Grothendieck notes that the existence of the fine parameter β in terms of the coarse γ in general relies on foundations 'not yet established', while in the M_{0,3}/j-line case condition (1D) computes it explicitly. This is an early, explicit framing of how GT-type parameters are constrained by descent to M_{1,1}, but it is close to what Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura later worked out.
missed.quote: un calcul du ... "délicat" β (dont l'existence en général, en termes de γ, repose sur des fondements qui n'ont pas encore été établis...), en termes du paramètre "grossier" γ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for the idea that GT elements must commute with the λ → j orbifold map; only modest mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine group-theoretic computation, (4∞) τ'_∞(ρ) = ρ^{-1}, inside a known programme: the GT action compatible with PSL_2(Z) is now in the literature. It is historically interesting as an early unpublished treatment but contains no evident unknown result.
transcription_corrections: Title likely 'Calcul de x = l_∞' (page number 422 at top; archive page 242).
'qui sont normalisés [?]' probably reads 'qui sont normalisants' or similar; meaning: elements normalizing L_0.
'variation [?]' in the correction above the struck word is likely 'paramètre' or 'variable' (delicate parameter β).
'Z/nZ [?]' inserted above 'lui-même' is uncertain; it could be a symbol like 'α_3' or 'μ'.
In the final formula, τ'_∞(φ) should be τ'_∞(ρ); underbraces: τ_∞ρ = l_0^{-1}ρ, l_0^{-1} ↦ ε_0^{-1}, σ_∞(ρ) = σ_∞ρσ_∞^{-1} = σ_∞^{-1} (with ε_0 under the last brace).
